sentence: This project uses digital phenotyping technology to study how online media, including substance-related content, affects adolescent use of drugs and alcohol.
This project makes stem cell lines from people with Alzheimer’s disease and related disorders, using gene editing, to study how risk genes affect human cells.
This project studies how genes in one pathway act to suppress tumors in small cell lung cancer.
This project makes fly and mouse models of human disease variants, then uses them to check how variants cause disease and to test possible treatments.
This project tries to deliver agents that change gene expression to neurons in the brain by attaching them to antibodies that cross the blood-brain barrier.
This project studies what causes ictal onset patterns in epilepsy, whether they predict outcomes after implant placement, and trains artificial neural networks to classify them.
This project builds a test of immunity to a seasonal betacoronavirus and a protocol for a controlled human infection model.
This project maps DNA damage across the genome to test whether two types of damage are linked to mutations in human liver and esophageal cancers.
This project studies weak points in glucose metabolism in diffuse midline gliomas, a brain cancer in children, that could be used for therapy and imaging.
This project uses proteomics, metabolomics and imaging mass spectrometry to find protein, lipid and metabolite changes in gastric cells and bacterial cells in gastric cancer.
This project tries to find out how kidney endothelial cells and tubules are injured in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury.
This project studies how a receptor for dopamine is activated and how it works in cocaine use disorder.
This project runs tests on how HIV infects cells and copies itself, to check ideas that come from structural information.
This project tests whether faulty splicing of RNA makes protein forms that affect immune interactions and drive myelodysplastic syndromes.
This project uses single molecule methods to study how CRISPR, chromatin remodelers and DNA mismatch repair work.
This project uses chemical and genetic screens to find small molecule inhibitors and genes that control cellular senescence.
This project studies what causes subgenomic particles to form in adeno-associated virus gene therapy vectors and tries to reduce them.
This project studies how loss of cholesterol synthesis in the intestine increases stem cell growth and cholesterol excretion from the body.
This project uses mouse models to study how fission and fusion of mitochondria affect rod photoreceptor cells in the retina.
This project studies how wanting, liking and learning about food reward relate to binge-eating disorder in brain and behavior.
